patches.replace: dome parameters is unfalsifiable. A close reader might counter that the gap between ~950 AD and the millennial Revelation 20 target is only a 5% miss — why is that not impressive? The answer is that the theological t=0 anchor is itself non-unique. A 1000-year reign measured from the resurrection (c. AD 33) targets ~AD 1033; from Constantine's Edict of Milan (AD 313), ~AD 1313; from the Council of Nicaea (AD 325), ~AD 1325; from Theodosius's establishment of Christianity as state religion (AD 380), ~AD 1380. Even granting only the four mainstream historicist anchor points, the plausible target band is ~AD 1033–1380 — roughly 350 years wide. (Under amillennial or symbolic readings the 1000 years has no fixed start at all, making the band effectively unbounded.) Combined with the ~200–400 year recurrence interval for archaeomagnetic SAA-like episodes documented by Hare et al. (2018), hitting some recurrence somewhere inside that band is statistically near-certain by base rate. The dome's apparent ~50-year fit is selection of one recurrence inside a wide window, not a tight prediction. Independent of the scientific critique above

holes_addressed: WIN-023.c4 hole #2 (minor): verdict dismisses theological link as unfalsifiable but does not say WHY the 1000-year theological target band is loose — fixed by inserting the t=0-anchor-non-uniqueness clause with four candidate anchor dates (AD 33 resurrection, AD 313 Constantine, AD 325 Nicaea, AD 380 Theodosius) bracketing a ~350yr target band, plus the Hare 2018 recurrence-interval base-rate calculation that makes a hit-inside-the-band near-certain.
new_evidence_added: Four historicist millennial t=0 anchors with target dates: resurrection AD 33 → AD 1033; Constantine AD 313 → AD 1313; Nicaea AD 325 → AD 1325; Theodosius AD 380 → AD 1380. Target band ~AD 1033–1380 = ~350yr wide.
Hare et al. 2018 (doi:10.1002/2017GL076007) — 200–400yr recurrence interval for archaeomagnetic SAA-like episodes, used as the base-rate denominator that makes a hit-inside-the-band near-certain.

anticipated_objections.objection: You cherry-picked anchors favorable to your case; a fundamentalist literalist would insist the resurrection (AD 33) is the only legitimate t=0, narrowing the band drastically.
anticipated_objections.response: The clause concedes "even granting only the four mainstream historicist anchor points" — i.e., we steel-man the literalist by allowing the narrowest, earliest anchor and STILL find the band is ~350yr wide once Constantine/Nicaea/Theodosius are admitted as competing historicist starting points (which they have been in mainstream Christian eschatology since at least the 4th century). And the parenthetical also covers the amillennial/symbolic case for completeness. The objection narrows the band to a single date only if the entire historicist-vs-amillennial debate is dismissed, which the dome author has not done in any published material.

anticipated_objections.objection: Hare 2018 documents recurrences from ~425 to ~1550 CE; your "200-400yr recurrence interval" misreads the paper as a deterministic cycle when it actually describes a stochastic emergence pattern.
anticipated_objections.response: The clause uses "recurrence interval" not "deterministic cycle" — the same language Hare et al. use. A stochastic emergence pattern with mean recurrence 200-400yr inside a window 1100yr wide (~425-1550 CE) gives 3-5 expected events; selecting one to align with any 350yr target band carries near-certainty under reasonable assumptions about timing uniformity. The argument does not depend on cycle determinism.

anticipated_objections.objection: The 5% miss framing is a strawman — the dome author has never publicly used "5%" as the figure of merit.
anticipated_objections.response: The 5% framing is constructed as the strongest defender argument the curmudgeon's advocate_mode identified (50 / 1000 = 5%). We rebut the strongest available defense, not the weakest. Even if the dome author never frames it that way, a sophisticated apologist would, and the verdict must survive that defense.

kernel_of_truth: The dome does correctly identify that ~950 AD is a real archaeomagnetic event (Campuzano 2019 SHAWQ2k confirms emergence of the current reversed-flux patch in the late first millennium; Tarduno 2015 corroborates). And a millennial-anchor prediction is in principle falsifiable: if the data had shown formation ~AD 500 or ~AD 1500, the millennial match would have failed. We acknowledge both in the existing verdict text. The new clause adds the specific reason the surviving "tight fit" defense fails: the falsification window the defender implicitly invokes (~±50yr) is much narrower than the actual definitional band the theological anchor admits (~350yr historicist; unbounded under amillennial reading).
